prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client is exhausted/fails, the pending JSON-RPC request's caller is never notified and hangs forever — both PRs make the failure reach the waiting caller instead of dying silently inside `_handle_reconnection`. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client is exhausted/fails, the pending JSON-RPC request's caller is never notified and hangs forever — both PRs make the failure reach the waiting caller instead of dying silently inside `_handle_reconnection`. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 2395 is the smaller, more targeted fix: it keeps the existing retry/bail-out flow in `_handle_reconnection` and just adds the missing notification (constructs a JSONRPCError and sends it via `ctx.read_stream_writer`, guarded by `isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest)`), resolving the specific stuck request without affecting the rest of the session. It also removes the pre-existing `# pragma: no cover` on that branch, indicating the fix ships with test coverage for the previously-untested bail-out path, and upgrades the log call from debug to warning to reflect the real severity. 3098 instead raises a `StreamableHTTPError` that propagates through the anyio task group, requiring a new recursive `_unwrap_exception` helper just to dig the error back out of a `BaseExceptionGroup` on the caller side — a heavier-handed approach that would tear down the whole task group/session rather than resolving only the affected request, and its diff also carries an unrelated cleanup (dropping the `as _annotations` alias on the `__future__` import) suggesting a less tightly scoped changeset.

prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs modify the same `create_memory_object_stream`/`create_context_streams` call that sizes the stdio server's `write_stream` (a 0-capacity/rendezvous channel). The root issue is that a zero-buffer write stream can block a handler from queuing a message (e.g. a final response) while `stdout_writer` is still flushing an earlier one (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 exposes the buffer size as an opt-in `write_stream_buffer_size`/`read_stream_buffer_size` parameter defaulting to 0 (no behavior change unless a caller explicitly passes a nonzero value), while #2654 hardcodes the write_stream capacity to 1 so the deadlock is fixed out of the box for all existing callers. (2 PRs)

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: the WWW-Authenticate header parser used naive substring/space-based matching instead of properly tokenizing the header, causing incorrect parameter extraction when values contain commas inside quoted strings (or multiple challenges are present). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer for the WWW-Authenticate header, but #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips everything before the first space and then splits the remainder on top-level commas, implicitly assuming a single challenge/scheme in the header. #3041 first splits the full header into per-challenge segments (_split_www_authenticate_segments), then explicitly locates the segment(s) whose scheme is 'Bearer' via _extract_bearer_auth_params, so it correctly isolates Bearer's params even when the header contains multiple auth schemes (e.g. 'Basic realm=..., Bearer realm=...'). That case is mishandled by #3012's simpler single-pass split.

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2492 requires extending the `TokenStorage` protocol with new `get_oauth_metadata`/`set_oauth_metadata` methods, so the fix only takes effect once each storage backend implementation is updated to support them (defaults are no-ops). #3263 fixes the same cold-start gap without any interface change — it performs on-demand AS metadata discovery before a cold-start refresh, adds an issuer-binding check to validate the discovered metadata, and tracks an `eager_discovery_attempted` flag so it isn't re-probed on every refresh call. members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both PRs modify the same `create_memory_object_stream`/`create_context_streams` call that sizes the stdio server's `write_stream` (a 0-capacity/rendezvous channel). The root issue is that a zero-buffer write stream can block a handler from queuing a message (e.g. a final response) while `stdout_writer` is still flushing an earlier one (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 exposes the buffer size as an opt-in `write_stream_buffer_size`/`read_stream_buffer_size` parameter defaulting to 0 (no behavior change unless a caller explicitly passes a nonzero value), while #2654 hardcodes the write_stream capacity to 1 so the deadlock is fixed out of the box for all existing callers.

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both PRs modify the same `create_memory_object_stream`/`create_context_streams` call that sizes the stdio server's `write_stream` (a 0-capacity/rendezvous channel). The root issue is that a zero-buffer write stream can block a handler from queuing a message (e.g. a final response) while `stdout_writer` is still flushing an earlier one (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 exposes the buffer size as an opt-in `write_stream_buffer_size`/`read_stream_buffer_size` parameter defaulting to 0 (no behavior change unless a caller explicitly passes a nonzero value), while #2654 hardcodes the write_stream capacity to 1 so the deadlock is fixed out of the box for all existing callers.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer for the WWW-Authenticate header, but #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips everything before the first space and then splits the remainder on top-level commas, implicitly assuming a single challenge/scheme in the header. #3041 first splits the full header into per-challenge segments (_split_www_authenticate_segments), then explicitly locates the segment(s) whose scheme is 'Bearer' via _extract_bearer_auth_params, so it correctly isolates Bearer's params even when the header contains multiple auth schemes (e.g. 'Basic realm=..., Bearer realm=...').
